title: Confidence-gated hybrid execution matrix for mixed-precision inference
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a runtime decision matrix that stitches FP16/FP8/INT8 execution paths with a confidence-gated runtime fallback. The matrix should be driven by per-request and per-layer calibration signals plus a lightweight confidence estimator so we can opportunistically run quantized kernels but gracefully fall back to higher-precision kernels when accuracy risk is detected. Goal: reduce average token cost by 20-30% on quantizable workloads while keeping regression rate under 0.5% on held-out eval prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a decision matrix config that maps (model, sequence_length_bucket, quant_profile, layer_group) -> preferred execution path
Confidence estimator produced during forward pass with <2% added latency overhead for 99th percentile requests
End-to-end e2e accuracy regression on evaluation benchmark remains <= 0.5% compared to FP16 baseline
Average per-token cost reduction measured on production-like workload >= 20% for models that have INT8/FP8 profiles
Canary rollout mechanism exists with traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regression signals
calibration_workflow: Offline calibration job that produces per-layer scale/zero-point candidates for INT8 and FP8 profiles
Calibration artifacts include: per-layer activation histograms, outlier thresholds, and a ranked list of candidate quant scales
Upload calibration artifacts to model manifest; decision matrix uses these artifacts at runtime to select quant kernels
Periodic recalibration cadence (weekly) and on-schema-change triggers (model update, tokenizer change)
Calibration pipeline includes a small validation subset to estimate expected per-layer L2 and KL divergence metrics
runtime_dispatch_policy: Matrix keys: model_id, model_version_tag, seq_len_bucket, profile_name (e.g., int8-0, fp8-e2e), layer_group_id
Each matrix cell encodes: preferred_kernel (fp16|fp8|int8), confidence_threshold, max_quantization_attempts, fallback_kernel
Confidence estimator computes a lightweight per-token divergence proxy using prefix logits and cached KV stability heuristics
On confidence < threshold: immediately switch to fallback_kernel for the remainder of the sequence; on confidence marginal, enable per-layer selective upcast
Support for sticky per-request decision so we avoid oscillation (sticky TTL measured in tokens)
Graceful degrade: if a quant kernel OOMs or returns NaNs, mark cell as degraded and fallback without user-visible error
validation_plan: Unit tests for matrix lookup correctness and TTL sticky behavior
Synthetic microbenchmarks across seq_len buckets verifying decision latency (target: <0.5ms added per-request)
Offline accuracy validation: run held-out prompt sets across 10K samples comparing output similarity (BERTScore + logit-scale KL) to FP16 baseline
Shadow A/B on 5% of production traffic for 2 weeks capturing token-level diff, end-user quality metrics, and cost per request
Canary with progressive traffic ramp (1% -> 5% -> 20%) and automatic rollback when regression thresholds exceeded
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate in control plane to enable matrix for specific customers/models
Start with internal sandbox customers and non-critical models (low regulatory constraints)
Run shadow mode for initial 2 weeks collecting telemetry without changing kernel choices
Enable active fallback for 1% of traffic and monitor quality signals for 7 days
If stable, expand to 20% and then to 100% with continued monitoring and periodic recalibration
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight decision cache keyed by (model, version, request_prefix_hash) to avoid repeated matrix lookups for long-lived sessions
Integrate calibration artifacts into model manifest and expose an API for the runtime to fetch latest artifact atomically
Leverage existing kernel abstraction layer; implement kernel adapters for FP8/INT8 that expose diagnostic counters
Keep confidence estimator off the critical path for common low-risk requests by using a sampling-based estimator initially
Work closely with infra to ensure candidate quant kernels are scheduled on compatible devices and memory pools
test_cases: TC-01: Short prompts (<=64 tokens) should prefer int8 when confidence > 0.9 and show cost reduction >=18%
TC-02: Long prompts (>=1024 tokens) should avoid aggressive int8 on specific layer groups where calibration shows heavy outliers
TC-03: Introduce synthetic outlier token (rare token sequence) and ensure fallback triggers within 5 tokens of detection
TC-04: Simulate quant kernel OOM and verify request continues on fallback kernel without user-visible error
TC-05: Canary rollback triggers when regression_rate_on_eval_prompts exceeds 0.5% over 24h
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positive confidence triggers cause unnecessary fallbacks and lost cost savings -> Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds + sticky TTL
Risk: Calibration skew after tokenizer/model patch -> Mitigation: recalibration pipeline with CI trigger on model/version change
Risk: Telemetry volume increases -> Mitigation: sampled metrics and aggregation at runtime, configurable retention
Risk: Edge-case numeric divergence in FP8 kernels -> Mitigation: per-kernel diagnostic counters + fast rollout disable switch
